reason: REFUTED on measurement, on precedent, and on the fix. (1) The register claim is false as measured. Driving master.html and dumping every visible text node in DOM order, .b-gapNote is the SEVENTH statement on the guest phone, not the second: "Mara & Finn" (y=28), "79" (y=65, 96px), "days" , "Saturday 3 October 2026" (y=163, 20px), "Wedding day" (y=193), "Kept by Orla" (y=228), "Today is 16 July" (y=280), then the note at y=311. It renders at 15px in fore-0.62 - the declared type FLOOR, the lowest ink density any letter on the page is permitted - under a 96px numeral and a 20px date. What the document says first about the most important day of their life is "Mara & Finn / 79 days / Saturday 3 October 2026 / Wedding day". The finding's rhetorical weight rests entirely on a position and a prominence the artifact does not have. (2) The keepsake claim is false in the opposite direction. On print the note does NOT sit above seven moments: the sheet is two columns, the note is in the LEFT column at y=432 with "Behind you - 3 moments" directly beneath it, while the seven moments live in the RIGHT column starting at y=288 with "16 - Menu tasting at The Orchard - Sat 1 Aug". On the printed keepsake the first planned moment is 144px HIGHER on the page than the sentence said to sit above it. Same at desk and owner-flight (note x=187, measure x=587). Only on the single-column phone is it above the rows at all. (3) This is round 3's finding re-raised with no new evidence. `nothing-is-planned-above-seven-planned-things` was refuted for the same reason, and round 1's `nothing-is-planned-is-off-by-one` - the verdict that WROTE this string - ratified its register explicitly: "The note must stay a statement about the gap... the note names the emptiness, the tick names the thing." (4) The fix is direction C's rejected thesis, and worse. lock.md lists C's discarded idea as "leading the received artifact with the single next thing, rather than making a reader find it on the measure", and states for B that "what is next is a filled tick and the nearest item" - the measure, not a sentence. "The first moment is on 1 August." also prints the first row's own date a third time (the tick carries "Sat 1 Aug", the away column carries "16"), which is precisely the class the settled list already refuses: "filling it with the date duplicates the readout below it." (5) The fix removes the only caption the measure's hole has. The lock names the honest cost of a proportional measure as "holes in the page": between .b-origin and the first tick there is 209px of deliberate emptiness at desk and ~192px on the phone. The absence sentence is what explains that blank to a reader who would otherwise read it as a rendering fault. A positive restatement of the first date explains nothing about the empty stretch it sits beside. (6) It also breaks a live contract. At desk width .b-gapNote is not static copy - render-b.js:1207-1247 rewrites it on scroll to name whatever tick is at the top of the pane ("8 September - in 54 days"), and interaction-check.mjs:1915-1936 asserts that it changes and changes back. Its at-rest job is to name what is actually on screen at rest, which IS the empty stretch. Under the fix the at-rest string becomes another row-naming statement in the same grammar as the scrolled one, and the readout stops distinguishing "you are looking at a gap" from "you are looking at a moment". The exact string is additionally asserted at interaction-check.mjs:245 and :376. What remains is one word of taste with no argument attached: the finding offers no evidence that a guest misreads a sentence bounded by "until", sitting one line above "DAYS AWAY" and 250px above "16 - Menu tasting at The Orchard", with "Behind you - 3 moments" below it. Not a 9.5-bar defect.
sharpenedFix: Nothing to do. If a future round wants to soften the opener it must clear four bars this fix does not: it must still caption the hole the proportional measure deliberately leaves, must not restate the first row's date in the left column, must read correctly as the at-rest value of a live readout whose other value is "<date> - in N days", and must not lead the received artifact with the next thing, which the lock rejected with direction C.
